fullPassage:
Have you ever felt anxious about your own creativity? Do you blame yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come? The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. They believed that a "genius" was not a gifted person but a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s studio. The poet Ruth Stone described how, as a child working in the fields, she could feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air, shaking the earth under her feet. When it reached her, she had to race to the house to grab a pencil and write it down. The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just showing up at her desk every morning and working through boring routine. But ideas would come, mysteriously, when she was deeply engaged and immersed in the work. The message is clear: put your heart and soul into your work, and your genius will come.

When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Now, I prefer American football. I graduated in India with a computer science degree at 22, and now I’m a journalist and podcast host in the US. We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood is replaced over time, is it still the same ship? We are living examples of this paradox. So here is my advice. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.

questions.passage: The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. They believed that a "genius" was not a gifted person but a kind of divine assistant spirit __________ lived in the walls of an artist’s studio.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 a kind of divine assistant spirit을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ that: 선행사(spirit) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ② who: 사람 선행사용 → spirit은 사물/추상
❌ ④ which: 가능하나, 앞에 not A but B 구문에서 that이 더 자연스러움
det.tip: 선행사 + that/which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: The poet Ruth Stone described how, as a child working in the fields, she could feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air, __________ the earth under her feet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절과 동시에 일어나는 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문 shaking이 적절하다. "시처럼 다가오면서 발밑의 땅을 흔들며"
det.analysis:
✅ ④ shaking: 동시동작 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① shook: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ② shaken: 과거분사 → 수동 의미이므로 부적절
❌ ③ to shake: to부정사 → 동시동작 표현에 부적절
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작/부대상황): 주절, ~ing ... → 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작

questions.passage: Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood __________ over time, is it still the same ship? We are living examples of this paradox.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목재가 교체되는 것이므로 수동태 is replaced가 적절하다. "모든 나무 조각이 시간이 지나면서 교체되면"
det.analysis:
✅ ② is replaced: 수동태 (목재가 교체되는 대상)
❌ ① replace: 능동 원형 → 주어(wood)가 교체하는 주체가 아님
❌ ③ will replace: 능동 미래 → 주어가 교체 주체가 아님
❌ ④ replacing: 현재분사 → if절 동사 자리에 부적절
det.tip: 주어가 동작을 당하는 경우 → 수동태(be + p.p.): wood is replaced = 나무가 교체되다

questions.passage: The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just __________ up at her desk every morning and working through boring routine. But ideas would come, mysteriously, when she was deeply engaged and immersed in the work.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 콜론(:) 뒤에서 앞의 process를 보충 설명하며, working과 병렬 구조를 이루는 동명사 showing이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② showing: 동명사 → "just showing up ... and working ..."으로 병렬
❌ ① show: 원형 → just 뒤에 동명사가 자연스러움
❌ ③ to have shown: 완료 부정사 → 문맥과 불일치
❌ ④ having shown: 완료 동명사 → 반복 일상에 부적절
❌ ⑤ showed: 과거형 → 콜론 뒤 보충설명에 부적절
det.tip: just + ~ing: "그저 ~하는 것" → 동명사로 행위를 설명

questions.passage: When it ①<u>reached</u> her, she had to race to the house to grab a pencil and write it down. The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just ②<u>showed</u> up at her desk every morning and ③<u>working</u> through boring routine.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② showed → showing: 콜론 뒤에서 process를 설명하는 동명사 구문이므로 working과 병렬을 이루는 showing이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② showed(과거형) → showing(동명사): working과 병렬 구조
✅ ① reached: 과거형 동사 → 시간절에서 올바름
✅ ③ working: 동명사 → showing과 병렬
det.tip: 병렬 구조: A and B → 같은 형태(동명사 + 동명사)로 맞춰야 함

❌ ② an artistic technique: 언급 없음
❌ ④ a thunderous poem: Ruth Stone 이야기에 해당
det.tip: not A but B 구문: A가 아니라 B → 빈칸은 B에 해당하는 내용

questions.passage: Have you ever felt __________ (anxiety) about your own creativity? Do you blame yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: anxiety(명사) → anxious(형용사): "felt + 형용사" 구문에서 감정 상태를 나타내는 형용사가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
anxiety(명사) → anxious(형용사)
felt + 형용사: "~하게 느꼈다"
felt anxious = 불안하게 느꼈다
det.tip: feel + 형용사: anxious(불안한), nervous(긴장한), excited(흥분한) 등 감정형용사

det.korean: mystery(명사) → mysteriously(부사): 동사 come을 수식하는 부사가 필요. "신비롭게 떠오르다"
det.analysis:
mystery(명사) → mysterious(형용사) → mysteriously(부사)
동사 come을 수식하는 부사 위치
mysteriously = 신비롭게
det.tip: mystery → mysterious → mysteriously — 명사 → 형용사 → 부사

questions.passage: We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood is replaced over time, is it still the same ship? We are living examples of this paradox. So here is my advice. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The speaker advises that we should hold on to our current opinions because our future self will agree with them."

det.korean: 본문: "your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others" → 미래의 자신이 현재 의견에 동의하지 않을 수 있으므로 타인을 존중하라고 함. "현재 의견을 고수하라"는 반대. → False
det.analysis:
❌ False: "may disagree" → 미래의 자신이 동의하지 않을 수 있음 ≠ "will agree"
"be respectful" → 고수가 아니라 열린 태도를 권함
det.tip: disagree(동의하지 않다) ≠ agree(동의하다) — 진술의 핵심 동사를 본문과 정확히 대조
